realLifeExampleSummary: Nach der Wahl zwischen zwei ähnlich guten Kopfhörern wirkt das gewählte Modell plötzlich besser und das abgelehnte schlechter.
coverHeadline: WARUM REDEN WIR UNS DAS SCHÖN?
coverVisualThesis: One buyer protects the chosen blue headphones while still glancing toward a similarly appealing rejected green pair, making post-choice doubt visible without introducing a second human species.

flowTextMoments.text: WARUM REDEN WIR UNS DAS SCHÖN?

scenes.speechSection: Warum verteidigst du manchmal eine Entscheidung besonders stark, obwohl du selbst noch Zweifel daran hast?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A person can visibly defend a choice while still being drawn to the rejected alternative.
scenes.observableEvidence: In an electronics store, one young adult buyer clutches chosen blue headphones and a receipt close to the torso while glancing sideways toward a similarly appealing green pair on display. No second person is needed.
scenes.representationReason: The hook depends on posture and gaze after a choice, so one human reaction is the clearest evidence; removing the friend also reduces same-frame species drift risk.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen item is physically protected while attention still returns to the rejected alternative.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No glowing brain, split head or abstract conflict energy.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Opening social/product conflict; establishes the choice in a store with one character rather than a generic object board.

scenes.speechSection: Eine mögliche Erklärung ist kognitive Dissonanz.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The viewer learns the mechanism name in a visually different purchase-aftermath composition.
scenes.observableEvidence: Top-down purchase aftermath with a crumpled receipt, plain shopping bag and only a cropped edge of the chosen blue headphones; the exact term is large and dominant. The rejected green pair is absent.
scenes.representationReason: The concept name is the information, so a sparse text-object composition is clearer than repeating the store character shot.
scenes.dominantRelation: Concept term is tied to the aftermath of a completed purchase rather than another product comparison.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No cracked head, lightning bolt or surreal mind symbol.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Moves from a medium-close store character to a top-down object/text aftermath with no rejected product visible.

scenes.speechSection: Sie beschreibt eine unangenehme Spannung, wenn Überzeugungen, Entscheidungen oder Verhalten nicht gut zusammenpassen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The completed decision and lingering urge to undo it can coexist in one concrete moment.
scenes.observableEvidence: At a home desk, the chosen blue headphones sit half outside a shopping bag beside the receipt and an open plain return box; one cropped stickman hand hesitates between lifting the headphones to use them and placing them back into the box.
scenes.representationReason: One real post-purchase action shows mismatch more clearly than a multi-stage schema.
scenes.dominantRelation: Use the chosen product versus repack it for return.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No diagram, brain icon, split screen or abstract energy.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Changes location from store/purchase graphics to a real home desk and changes the object state to half-used versus returnable.

scenes.speechSection: Du stehst zum Beispiel zwischen zwei ähnlich guten Kopfhörern, kaufst Modell A und lässt Modell B liegen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A difficult everyday choice between similar products creates the post-choice setup.
scenes.observableEvidence: Top-down electronics counter with two equally prominent generic over-ear headphones, matte blue and muted green, while one simplified stickman hand reaches decisively for the blue pair.
scenes.representationReason: The choice itself is the point; the products and selecting hand communicate it faster than another full character.
scenes.dominantRelation: One of two similarly attractive alternatives is selected.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No brands, prices or packaging words.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Returns to the purchase moment but uses a direct top-down two-object decision instead of the prior home-return scene.

scenes.speechSection: Danach fallen dir plötzlich besonders die Vorteile von A und die Nachteile von B auf.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: After choosing, attention can shift toward favorable details of the chosen option and flaws in the rejected one.
scenes.observableEvidence: Two-state macro comparison only: left, blue ear padding and sturdy build under close inspection; right, the green pair's small ordinary hinge flaw under close inspection. Only cropped hands if needed.
scenes.representationReason: The sentence explicitly contrasts positive versus negative feature attention, so a restrained two-state macro comparison is appropriate.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen product receives favorable inspection while rejected product receives critical inspection.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No thumbs, stars, scores, labels or third panel.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Shifts from full products to extreme macro detail and changes the action from choosing to selectively inspecting features.

scenes.speechSection: Genau solche Veränderungen nach Entscheidungen untersuchte Jack Brehm bereits 1956.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Post-decision evaluation shifts were tested experimentally decades ago.
scenes.observableEvidence: A wide 1950s psychology research room with period household items on a table; one participant evaluates them while a researcher records responses on a clipboard.
scenes.representationReason: The historical study setup is the evidence, so the room and props should carry the frame.
scenes.dominantRelation: Participant evaluates consumer alternatives in a controlled 1950s setting.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No modern devices or readable brands.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Breaks the modern headphone run entirely with a wide historical environment and new household-item set.

scenes.speechSection: Nach einer Wahl wurde das gewählte Produkt oft positiver und das abgelehnte negativer bewertet als zuvor.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The chosen and rejected alternatives can move apart in later evaluation.
scenes.observableEvidence: One physical 1950s research-table scene: two product cards sit on a wooden ranking tray after the choice; the chosen card has just been moved one position higher and the rejected card one lower, while two neutral wooden markers remain at their former nearly equal positions.
scenes.representationReason: A single physical rearrangement shows the evaluation shift without a three-stage explainer board.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen and rejected item positions separate from their former near-equal positions.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No numbers, percentages, labels, charts or timeline panels.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Moves from the wide lab to a tight physical measurement detail and replaces a timeline with one decisive action.

scenes.speechSection: Diese Verschiebung wird häufig als eine Form von Dissonanzreduktion nach einer Entscheidung interpretiert.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The interpretation concerns what happens after the choice, not a literal mental-energy event.
scenes.observableEvidence: Wider 1950s research-room aftermath: the participant walks toward the exit carrying the selected household item while the rejected item remains on the table near the separated ranking cards; the researcher stays by the arrangement.
scenes.representationReason: A real after-choice consequence in the historical room is clearer and less repetitive than another ranking-board comparison.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen item leaves with the participant while rejected item and separated ratings remain behind.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No brain icons or abstract energy.
scenes.camera: wide room aftermath with foreground research table
scenes.visualChangeReason: Changes from tight tabletop evidence to a wide spatial consequence with participant movement and room depth.

scenes.speechSection: Ein zweiter Klassiker von Festinger und Carlsmith aus dem Jahr 1959 untersuchte erzwungene Zustimmung.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A different classic paradigm used a deliberately monotonous task and social statement.
scenes.observableEvidence: A late-1950s psychology lab with repetitive wooden peg-and-spool apparatus, stopwatch, plain chairs and a waiting area visible through an open doorway.
scenes.representationReason: The distinctive task and period lab establish the new paradigm better than another product scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: A visibly tedious repetitive task sits at the center of the lab.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable study title or modern electronics.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Starts a new experimental world with different objects, era-specific task and doorway depth.

scenes.speechSection: Teilnehmende erledigten eine langweilige Aufgabe und sollten danach einer anderen Person sagen, sie sei interessant.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Participants publicly described a dull task positively to another person.
scenes.observableEvidence: At the lab doorway, one participant uses deliberately upbeat hand gestures toward a waiting participant while the boring peg apparatus remains visible behind them. Both figures use identical approved stickman base anatomy.
scenes.representationReason: The social statement itself is the evidence, so human interaction is necessary.
scenes.dominantRelation: Positive social presentation conflicts with the visibly dull task behind the speaker.
scenes.camera: medium doorway interaction with lab depth
scenes.visualChangeReason: Moves from empty lab setup to a medium human interaction centered on behavior rather than apparatus alone.

scenes.speechSection: Wer dafür nur einen kleinen Anreiz bekam, bewertete die Aufgabe später positiver als Teilnehmende mit einem großen Anreiz.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The classic result contrasted small versus large incentive conditions.
scenes.observableEvidence: Two-state comparison only: left, a participant receives one small reward token and later gives a mildly positive evaluation gesture; right, another participant receives a thick cash envelope and remains visibly unimpressed. Both sides use the exact same base stickman species.
scenes.representationReason: The claim directly contrasts two conditions, so a two-state comparison is the clearest representation.
scenes.dominantRelation: Small external incentive is paired with a more positive later evaluation than a large external incentive.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No exact dollar amounts, scores, forms, headings or third panel.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Changes from one doorway interaction to an explicit two-condition comparison with reward objects as the focal difference.

scenes.speechSection: Die klassische Erklärung: Bei geringer äußerer Rechtfertigung passten Verhalten und eigene Einstellung schlechter zusammen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A tiny external reward sits beside behavior that publicly presents the dull task positively.
scenes.observableEvidence: One coherent lab scene: a single small reward token lies foreground-large on the table; in the middle ground the participant makes upbeat gestures to the waiting person at the doorway while the dull peg task remains visible behind them. No panels or diagram.
scenes.representationReason: Putting weak incentive, positive statement and dull task into one physical space shows the classic logic without an overloaded explainer board.
scenes.dominantRelation: Tiny reward in foreground versus strongly positive public behavior with boring task visible behind.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No brain icons, scales, labels, arrows or multi-panel sequence.
scenes.camera: deep single-scene composition from reward token to doorway
scenes.visualChangeReason: Replaces the previous two-state condition comparison with one deep real-space causal relation; no repeated panels.

scenes.speechSection: Eine Möglichkeit, diese Spannung zu reduzieren, ist die eigene Bewertung nachträglich zu verändern.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: One possible response is to change how the chosen option is evaluated afterward.
scenes.observableEvidence: At home, the blue headphones sit prominently on the desk while one hand closes an unreadable comparison page containing only a small cropped image of the green alternative; the receipt stays nearby.
scenes.representationReason: Object handling and placement show the rejected alternative being put away without another argument scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen product is brought forward while the rejected comparison is closed away.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable web text or scores.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Returns to the modern story after the historical section, with a new home context and closing-away action rather than another store display.

scenes.speechSection: Aber Dissonanztheorie ist kein Gedankenleser: Nicht jede Rechtfertigung oder Meinungsänderung lässt sich damit erklären.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Opinions can change because of real new evidence, not only dissonance reduction.
scenes.observableEvidence: Tight close-up of the chosen blue headphones with a clearly broken hinge; one hand turns the damaged joint beside the receipt.
scenes.representationReason: A concrete external defect cleanly shows an alternative reason for reevaluation.
scenes.dominantRelation: New physical damage provides a direct reason to change evaluation.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No labels or symbolic brain imagery.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Changes the recurring blue product into a physically damaged state and tightens to an extreme macro counterexample.

scenes.speechSection: Moderne Übersichten diskutieren weiterhin Messprobleme, unterschiedliche Paradigmen und offene theoretische Fragen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Modern dissonance research uses varied paradigms and still faces measurement/theory questions.
scenes.observableEvidence: Wide modern social-psychology workspace with separate simple task setups on different tables, blank questionnaires and two researchers comparing materials. Both researchers use identical approved stickman base anatomy.
scenes.representationReason: Methodological variety is best shown by a real research environment rather than another text card.
scenes.dominantRelation: Different experimental setups coexist without one universal measurement apparatus.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable paper titles, charts or statistics.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Leaves the product story for a wide contemporary research context with multiple real setups and strong spatial depth.

scenes.speechSection: Wenn du eine Wahl plötzlich extrem verteidigst, lohnt sich die Frage:
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The viewer gets a short visual pause before the final self-check question.
scenes.observableEvidence: Quiet present-day desk close-up: the chosen blue headphones sit beside the receipt while one hand rests on the edge of the desk; the rejected green alternative is only a small blurred shape farther back, leaving clear negative space for a reflective beat without readable text.
scenes.representationReason: Splitting the final 21-word sentence prevents an overly long static text frame and creates a concrete visual pause before the closing question.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen item is foreground-clear while the rejected option recedes, creating a moment of reconsideration.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No text, question mark icon or thought bubble.
scenes.camera: quiet close desk composition with negative space
scenes.visualChangeReason: Changes from a wide research workspace to an intimate modern desk close-up and intentionally pauses before the final text card.

scenes.speechSection: Überzeugt sie mich – oder beruhige ich gerade meine Entscheidung?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The final reflection distinguishes conviction from post-choice self-justification.
scenes.observableEvidence: Top-down illustrated desk with the chosen blue headphones, purchase receipt and a small cropped image of the rejected green alternative framing one large note card with the exact final question.
scenes.representationReason: The final clause is explicitly a reflective question, so a short dedicated text frame is stronger and faster than holding one text card through the full closing sentence.
scenes.dominantRelation: The final question sits between the chosen object and the evidence of the rejected alternative.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No extra labels or explanatory paragraph.
scenes.visualChangeReason: Moves from a no-text close reflective pause to one short, large final text card, avoiding a long static hold.
